outcome: Negative emotions during birth (guilt and fear)
cohort: Pregnant women (N=1833) recruited at community and hospital medical centers in Israel and through internet forums.
finding: Skin-to-skin contact after birth was associated with reduced negative emotions during birth, particularly guilt and fear, especially among women who had cesarean sections, which mediated the relationship between mode of birth and PTSS-FC.
mod_finding: Skin-to-skin contact was associated with reduced negative emotions during birth, particularly guilt and fear, especially among women who had cesarean sections.
